acceptance.given: A TC-D1 governance write authorization evaluates a proposed path that belongs to an account boundary, with replay and Consumer permissions potentially present.

oracle.expected: The governance policy deterministically rejects the account-boundary write, identifies the protected account boundary, and grants no authorization regardless of replay or Consumer permission.
forbidden: A write to an account boundary is authorized.
Replay evidence or Consumer permission authorizes account repair.
A runtime outcome is accepted without checking the protected-path classification.
oracle.observable: The governance-policy result contains a rejected decision for the account-boundary path, a protected-boundary diagnostic, and no authorization grant.

acceptance.then: Current validator evidence binds the rejected path, protected-boundary classification, policy inputs, and absence of an authorization override.
acceptance.when: A TC-D1 write targets an account path.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the governance-policy unit tests with an account-boundary target and report a contract violation if the proposed write is accepted instead of rejected.

Run the governance-policy unit tests with replay and Consumer permission inputs enabled for an account-boundary target and report a binding failure if either permission changes the protected-boundary rejection.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or verify a Toolchain governance-policy decision that classifies account-boundary paths as protected and rejects writes independently of replay evidence or Consumer permission.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing governance-policy API and fail-closed behavior; rollback restores the prior protected account-boundary rejection and never authorizes account writes.

slice_hint.state_transition: Proposed account-boundary write -> protected account-boundary classification -> deterministic rejection with no replay or Consumer override.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The governance validator returns an unsuccessful result for every account-boundary write attempt, emits the protected-boundary diagnostic, and returns the same rejection when replay or Consumer permissions are supplied.
